summary: Reproduced Bug A in the checked-out implementation: the standard JPEG GPU-decode call omitted ImageReadMode.RGB, so a grayscale decode remained one-channel, failed mixed-image stacking, and produced 256-wide Gemma-4-style patches for a 768-input projection. The narrow fix explicitly requests RGB from torchvision. Bug B (scheduler blast radius) was not changed or qualified.

tests.what_was_measured: Before: recorded the implementation calling decode_jpeg with only device=cuda, grayscale/RGB shapes (1,48,64)/(3,48,64), mixed-stack failure, and the gfx950 matmul failure (12x256 and 768x1152). After: recorded explicit ImageReadMode.RGB, both shapes (3,48,64), successful stacking, and a gfx950 projection result of (12,1152). Raw logs: reproduction-before.log and reproduction-after.log.
12 focused image-decoding tests passed, including grayscale-to-RGB normalization, unchanged RGB channel count, and mixed grayscale/RGB stackability. Raw output: unit-tests.log.
All applicable repository formatting, lint, security, and test-registration hooks passed. Raw output: pre-commit.log.

Confirmed the assigned device is AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 and captured the environment limitation: this torchvision build raises 'not compiled with nvJPEG support'. Raw output: nvjpeg-gfx950-limitation.log.

gpu_evidence: On HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 identified AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. The pre-fix Gemma-4-shaped Linear(768,1152) projection failed on-device for 256-wide grayscale patches; after RGB normalization it succeeded with output shape (12,1152).
remaining_limitations: The ROCm torchvision build lacks nvJPEG, so the real standard GPU JPEG decoder could not run on gfx950; the checked-out _load_image control flow and decoder arguments were tested deterministically by substituting torchvision's CPU decoder at that boundary.
Gemma-4 weights and the reported 2xH200 TP=2 environment were unavailable, so no full model or HTTP serving reproduction is claimed.
The scheduler blast-radius Bug B and true per-request isolation were not changed or verified; this PR is limited to Bug A, consistent with the upstream maintainer request to split the fixes.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source was changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
